# Introduction

`smoothclust` is a method for identification of spatial domains and spatially-aware clustering in spatial transcriptomics data. The method generates spatial domains with smooth boundaries by smoothing gene expression profiles across neighboring spatial locations, followed by unsupervised clustering. Spatial domains consisting of consistent mixtures of cell types may then be further investigated by applying cell type compositional analyses or differential analyses.


# Installation

The `smoothclust` package can be installed from Bioconductor as follows (using R version 4.4 onwards). This is the recommended installation for most users. Additional details are shown on the [Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/packages/smoothclust) package page.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("smoothclust")
```

The latest development version of the package can also be installed from the [devel](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/use-devel.html) version of Bioconductor or from [GitHub](https://github.com/lmweber/smoothclust).


# Input data format

Input data can be provided either as a [SpatialExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/SpatialExperiment) object within the Bioconductor framework, or as numeric matrices of expression values and spatial coordinates. See help file (`?smoothclust`) for details.

In the example workflow below, we assume the input is in `SpatialExperiment` format.


# Tutorial

The example workflow in this section demonstrates how to run `smoothclust` to generate spatial domains with smooth boundaries for a dataset from the 10x Genomics Visium platform.

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(smoothclust)
library(STexampleData)
library(scran)
library(scater)
library(ggspavis)
```


Load dataset from `STexampleData` package:

```{r}
# load data
spe <- Visium_humanDLPFC()

# keep spots over tissue
spe <- spe[, colData(spe)$in_tissue == 1]

dim(spe)
assayNames(spe)
```


Filtering is performed outside `smoothclust`, using the raw counts. First, we
identify mitochondrial genes and calculate spot-level quality-control (QC)
metrics from the complete count matrix. QC thresholds should be selected for
each dataset or sample; for this compact example, we retain tissue spots with
positive total and non-mitochondrial counts.

```{r}
# calculate QC metrics from complete raw counts
raw_counts <- assay(spe, "counts")
is_mito <- grepl("(^mt-)", rowData(spe)$gene_name, ignore.case = TRUE)

total_counts <- Matrix::colSums(raw_counts)
detected_genes <- Matrix::colSums(raw_counts > 0)
mito_counts <- Matrix::colSums(raw_counts[is_mito, , drop = FALSE])
non_mito_counts <- total_counts - mito_counts

colData(spe)$sum <- total_counts
colData(spe)$detected <- detected_genes
colData(spe)$percent_mito <- 100 * mito_counts / total_counts

summary(colData(spe)[, c("sum", "detected", "percent_mito")])
table(is_mito)

# illustrative spot-level QC
keep_spot <- total_counts > 0 & non_mito_counts > 0
spe <- spe[, keep_spot]
raw_counts <- raw_counts[, keep_spot, drop = FALSE]
```


We calculate library size factors from all non-mitochondrial genes before
low-expression filtering. This keeps normalization independent of the chosen
expression threshold while preventing mitochondrial composition from affecting
normalization of the retained genes.

```{r}
# calculate non-mitochondrial size factors before gene filtering
non_mito_library_sizes <- Matrix::colSums(
    raw_counts[!is_mito, , drop = FALSE]
)
size_factors <- non_mito_library_sizes / mean(non_mito_library_sizes)

summary(size_factors)
```


Next, we apply an illustrative low-expression filter and remove mitochondrial
genes. Filtering rules are study-specific; here, we retain genes detected in at
least five spots. A spot may have zero counts across the retained genes after
this feature filtering. Such spots can remain in the input because we supply
positive size factors calculated from the broader, unfiltered gene set.

```{r}
# filter low-expressed and mitochondrial genes
keep_expressed <- Matrix::rowSums(raw_counts > 0) >= 5
keep_gene <- keep_expressed & !is_mito
spe <- spe[keep_gene, ]

dim(spe)
```


Run `smoothclust` using default parameter settings, which have been selected to be appropriate for Visium data from human tissue. By default, `smoothclust` normalizes the raw counts using library size factors, smooths the normalized values, and then applies a log-transformation. Supplying the factors calculated above ensures that normalization is defined using all non-mitochondrial genes rather than only the filtered analysis features.

The method for smoothing can be specified by providing the `method` argument, with available options `uniform`, `kernel`, and `knn`. Additional arguments can be used to set parameter values, including `bandwidth`, `k,` and `truncate`, depending on the choice of method. For more details, see the function documentation (`?smoothclust`).

```{r, results="hide"}
# run smoothclust using default parameters
spe <- smoothclust(spe, size_factors = size_factors)
```


The normalized, smoothed, and log-transformed expression values are stored in a
new assay named `logcounts_smooth`:

```{r}
# check output object
assayNames(spe)
```


Run clustering. We use a clustering workflow adapted from standard single-cell workflows. We select highly variable genes (HVGs) from smoothed log-expression by ranking residual variance above a fitted mean–variance trend using `modelGeneVar()`. These residuals provide empirical feature-ranking scores for clustering. We then perform k-means clustering on the top principal components (PCs) calculated from the selected genes.

We use a relatively small number of clusters for demonstration purposes in this example:

```{r}
# preprocessing steps for clustering

# select top highly variable genes (HVGs)
dec <- modelGeneVar(spe, assay.type = "logcounts_smooth")
top_hvgs <- getTopHVGs(dec, prop = 0.1)
length(top_hvgs)
```

```{r}
# dimensionality reduction

# compute PCA on top HVGs
set.seed(123)
spe <- runPCA(
    spe,
    subset_row = top_hvgs,
    exprs_values = "logcounts_smooth"
)
```

```{r}
# run k-means clustering
set.seed(123)
k <- 5
clust <- kmeans(reducedDim(spe, "PCA"), centers = k)$cluster
table(clust)
colLabels(spe) <- factor(clust)
```


Plot clusters / spatial domains generated by the smoothclust workflow:

```{r}
# color palettes
pal8 <- "libd_layer_colors"
pal36 <- unname(palette.colors(36, "Polychrome 36"))

# plot clusters / spatial domains
plotCoords(spe, annotate = "label", pal = pal8)
```


Plot manually annotated reference labels, which can be used to evaluate the performance of the clustering in this dataset:

```{r}
# plot reference labels
plotCoords(spe, annotate = "ground_truth", pal = pal8)
```


# Boundary density

`boundary_density()` uses its own `k` argument for the number of neighbors, independently of smoothing. For example:

```{r}
boundary_k <- c(2L, 6L, 18L)
vapply(boundary_k, function(k_i) {
    boundary_density(spatialCoords(spe), colLabels(spe), k = k_i)$boundary_density
}, numeric(1))
```
